annotationRationale: Independence gives each tie probability, and disjoint addition produces a convergent geometric series. Taking the complement and exchanging the colors gives the requested probability.
sourceMethod: Follows the official method of summing same-bin probabilities, taking the complement, and dividing equally between the two orders by symmetry.

review.mathCheck: Independence gives tie probability 4^(−k) in bin k. Summing the convergent geometric series gives 1/3. The remaining probability 2/3 splits equally between the two strict orders by color symmetry, yielding 1/3, choice C. All outcomes are accounted for.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of official solution 17 on page 7: sum equal-bin probabilities, take the complement, and halve by symmetry. The candidate explicitly explains independence, disjointness and convergence.
review.annotationCheck: Infinite geometric summation, complement and independence are appropriately assessed; disjoint addition supports the tie calculation. Color symmetry is clearly justified.
